questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why so many people believe in ghosts and spirits
The making of a famous Disney movie about the sea
Different stories about mermaids around the world
How frogs are able to live on land and in water
questions.why: They discuss mermaids, which feature in myths and legends of many cultures.

questions.q: What did the Sirens do in the ancient Greek story?
options: Their singing led to a shipwreck
They saved Odysseus from drowning in a storm
They married sailors
They protected the water kingdom
questions.why: Georgina says their seductive singing shipwrecked Odysseus and his sailors.

questions.q: How is Disney's Ariel different from the Sirens?
options: She is dangerous and seductive like them
She can't sing
She lives on land
She is defenceless, not dangerous
questions.why: Neil says Ariel seems the total opposite of the seductive, dangerous Sirens.

questions.q: According to Marcelle Mateki, what role does Mami Wata usually have?
options: She attacks fishermen
She protects the water kingdom
She teaches children to swim
She brings rain to farmers
questions.why: She says Mami Wata is commonly seen as the protector of the water kingdom.

questions.q: What can Selkies from the Orkney Islands do?
options: Become human, marry, then return to the sea
Fly between the islands at night looking for food
Sing beautiful songs to sink passing ships
Turn fishermen into fish with a magic spell
questions.why: Georgina says Selkies can take human form and marry men, but return to the sea now and then.

questions.q: According to Cristina Bacchilega, what do these different mermaid stories make us think about?
options: How to catch more fish from the sea
Which culture has the best stories
Our link with nature and ourselves
Why children like fairy tales
questions.why: Neil says they force us to question our relationship to water and nature and how we see ourselves.

questions.q: What does Cristina Bacchilega suggest humans should show towards the natural world?
options: Fear
Humility
Control
Pride
questions.why: She asks whether we approach this world with humility or with a human-centred view.

questions.q: What does Georgina mean when she compares mermaids to electricity?
options: Mermaids are dangerous like electricity
She has seen both of them
Electricity was discovered by the sea
Not seeing something doesn't prove it isn't real
questions.why: She says she's never seen a mermaid, but she's never seen electricity either, and believes in that.
